title: SIK3 controls synaptic localization of NMDA receptors by phosphorylating GluN1
title_zh: SIK3通过磷酸化GluN1控制NMDA受体的突触定位
abstract: Synaptic NMDA-type glutamate receptors (NMDARs) are central components of all neural computations. NMDAR levels critically vary between synapses but how the synaptic localization of NMDARs is controlled remains unclear. Here we show that SIK3, a serine-threonine protein kinase, localizes to synapses where it phosphorylates the obligatory NMDAR subunit GluN1 at a single site. This single phosphorylation event controls NMDAR recruitment to synapses. Genetic deletion of SIK3 severely and selectively decreases synaptic GluN1 levels by ~60% without altering AMPA-type glutamate receptor levels or inducing major transcriptional changes. Pharmacological inhibition of SIK3 impairs synaptic NMDAR responses within 45 minutes. Mutating the SIK3-phosphorylation site inhibits GluN1 synaptic recruitment. 'Sleepy', a gain-of-function mutation in SIK3 that increases sleep, selectively enhances synaptic NMDAR levels by increasing GluN1 phosphorylation. Thus, SIK3 phosphorylation of GluN1 provides a key signal for recruiting NMDARs to synapses.
abstract_zh: 突触NMDA型谷氨酸受体（NMDAR）是所有神经计算的核心组成部分。突触处NMDAR水平在突触间存在显著差异，但NMDAR突触定位的控制机制仍不清楚。本研究表明，SIK3是一种丝氨酸-苏氨酸蛋白激酶，定位于突触处，并特异性磷酸化必需的NMDAR亚基GluN1。这一单一磷酸化事件控制NMDAR的突触招募。SIK3的基因敲除显著且选择性地降低了突触GluN1水平约60%，而不改变α-氨基-3-羟基-5-甲基-4-异丙酸受体水平或诱导主要转录变化。SIK3的药理抑制在45分钟内即损害突触NMDAR电流。突变SIK3磷酸化位点会抑制GluN1的突触招募。'Sleepy'是SIK3获得功能突变，可增加睡眠，通过增加GluN1磷酸化选择性增强突触NMDAR水平。因此，SIK3对GluN1的磷酸化是将NMDAR招募至突触的关键信号。
